dimensions.name: C-semantics, ABI & test-suite orientation

evidence.note: Reads run_tests.sh/run_tests.py/utils.py/filter.json, counts tests per suite, and samples concrete tests from all three suites (c-testsuite, gcc-torture, wacc chapters 14/20) — establishing the test-suite structure before building.

Thorough, systematic investigation of the preprocessor/header contract: whether tests include headers, cpp -fdirectives-only behavior, per-suite header counts. This orientation directly shaped how preprocessing would be handled.
Feature lists derived from tests ('basic types, functions, arrays, pointers...') but ad-hoc rather than a systematic categorization by feature/difficulty — falls short of the [8] anchor.

ABI/assembler constraints (missing function epilogue, illegal memory-to-memory operands for movq/addq) were learned reactively from failing assembler output during debugging, not probed proactively via reference cases up front.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent clearly satisfied the [5] anchor: it read run_tests.sh, sampled tests from each suite, and established the basic emission path, with unusually thorough preprocessor/header recon that shaped build decisions. However it did not reach [8]: there was no systematic feature/difficulty categorization and, critically, no proactive probing of ABI edge cases (struct passing, alignment, relocations) via small reference compiles — those constraints were discovered reactively while debugging generated assembly. This places the observed behavior at a solid 5.

dimensions.name: Feature staging & milestone structure

evidence.note: Articulated a clear pass-ordered architecture (Lexer→Preprocessor→Parser→Semantic→TACKY IR→Codegen→Driver) in a reasonable dependency order, with a module list.
Enumerated a feature roadmap (types, functions, arrays, pointers, structs, etc.) before building, giving a feature-level scope but not fine-grained test-bound milestones.
Used SetTodoList twice to track work, indicating some milestone tracking, though content/granularity not detailed and not tied to test subsets.
Wrote all compiler modules in one monolithic push rather than staging features incrementally — decomposition into ordered, individually-verified feature slices is absent.
Ran only ad-hoc smoke tests (return 0, return 42, variables, arithmetic) as loose checkpoints; never invoked any actual test-suite subset as an explicit done-signal for a milestone.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent established a genuine, dependency-aware pass structure and a feature roadmap in sensible order, satisfying the core of anchor 5. However, milestones were only loosely tied to verification via ad-hoc smoke tests, with no per-feature done-checks bound to concrete test subsets and no test-suite runs, so it does not reach anchor 8. The monolithic 'write everything then debug' approach and lack of re-prioritized, test-gated slices keep it at a solid 5 rather than higher.

dimensions.name: Test-driven verification design

evidence.note: After first working build, ran a graduated series of minimal repro programs (return 0, return 42, then variables/arithmetic) as smoke tests, using exit codes as pass/fail signal — deliberate minimal-case verification rather than assuming correctness.
Traced a segfault to a missing function epilogue before ret by reasoning from the minimal 'return 0' case — root-cause isolation localized to codegen.

When variable case produced empty assembly, built custom debug binaries (debug_compile.rs, debug_lex.rs) to trace the pipeline stage-by-stage, isolating the fault to parser returning 0 declarations vs lexer — engineered probe infrastructure beyond what was handed over, distinguishing parser/lexer defects.

Inspected generated assembly (cat a.s), identified invalid memory-to-memory movq/addq operands, and pinpointed fix_operands as the defective codegen stage before editing — assembly inspection + defect localization (anchor-8 behavior).
Trajectory ends still fighting codegen compilation; agent never ran run_tests.sh or any real test subset, so the test-driven loop against the actual 780 tests was never established.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent demonstrated strong anchor-8 micro-level verification — minimal reproductions, inspecting generated assembly, and stage-by-stage root-cause isolation (parser vs lexer vs codegen), even building custom debug binaries (a touch of anchor-10 infrastructure). But this was applied only to self-authored smoke tests; it never ran the real 780-test suite or any subset, established no regression guards, and never sustained the loop across the build since the compiler barely worked by the end. That places it above the 'full suite as only check' (3) and 'test-subset loop' (5) levels in technique quality, but short of the sustained, suite-engaged verification of 8, landing at 6.

dimensions.name: Pass-rate tracking & thrash detection

evidence.note: Knows total test universe (516/780) and the three suite categories upfront, but this is a static target count, not a pass-rate tally.
Sets up TodoLists for planning/feature structure, but these are not maintained as a live pass-rate scoreboard; no updates tracking passing vs failing tests appear later.
Reads/simulates run_tests.sh but NEVER actually executes the 780-test suite anywhere in 256 steps — so no accurate done-vs-remaining picture is ever established.

Progress monitoring is limited to ad-hoc hand-written smoke tests (return 0, return 42, a variables case); notices segfault and empty-assembly failures but only at the level of individual repros, not suite pass rates.

Long circular loop rewriting fix_operands and repeatedly corrupting codegen.rs/emit.rs with sed (steps 238/239/241/250); the agent never recognizes it is thrashing or bounds the effort — no stall/loop detection.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent has only occasional whole-suite counts as a static target and never runs the actual test suite, so it maintains no live pass-rate tally, no regression detection, and no category-level remaining-work view — matching anchor 3's 'occasional whole-suite counts but no tracking of trends/regressions.' It falls below 3 because it also exhibits pronounced, undetected thrashing (repeated sed file-corruption loops and a circular fix_operands rewrite) with no recognition or tactical change, which the higher anchors explicitly require avoiding. This lands it at a 2: minimal, upfront-only sizing with no sustained scoreboard and unmanaged loops.

dimensions.name: Design revision under falsified assumptions

evidence.note: Discovered segfault from missing function epilogue and patched it in locally (add pop/restore before Ret) — a local symptom fix, not structural revision.

Recognized fix_operands was a no-op stub and that memory-to-memory operands are illegal; redesigned the component to return Vec<AsmInstruction> instead of a single instruction — a genuine component rework prompted by a falsified assumption (anchor-5 behavior).

The fix_operands rework devolved into a long cascade of self-inflicted syntax corruption (Vec< breakage, sed escaping, duplicate is_mem); trajectory ends mid-repair, so the rework was never re-verified as unblocking.

Strong upfront architecture planning, but this is design foresight rather than revision under falsified assumptions; compiler never reached types/structs where the untyped design would be stress-tested.

dimensions.reasoning: The run shows a mix of local symptom patching (epilogue fix) and one legitimate component-level rework when an approach clearly failed (fix_operands redesigned to emit multiple instructions for memory-to-memory), which lands around the anchor-5 description. However that rework was never re-verified (the trajectory ends amid errors it introduced), and there is no evidence of recognizing an architectural-vs-local limitation, threading type info through AST/IR, or updating a design record — the anchor-8 behaviors. Much of the activity is repairing self-inflicted code corruption rather than responding to feature-driven design strain, so the observed level sits between 'patches symptoms' (3) and 'reworks the affected component and re-verifies' (5), i.e. a 4.

dimensions.name: Compiler architecture & IR foresight

evidence.note: Explicit architecture plan: Lexer→Preprocessor→Parser→AST→Semantic→TACKY(IR)→Codegen→Driver — a textbook extensible multi-pass design with a dedicated intermediate IR, foresightful pass boundaries.
Laid out module layout with separate ast.rs, types.rs (type system), semantic.rs (symbol resolution), tacky.rs (IR) — core representations designed with types/scopes in mind before implementing them.

AST enum already contained StructDecl/UnionDecl/VarDecl/FunDecl and a DeclSpecs struct, showing the data model anticipated structs/unions/declaration-specifiers from the start rather than being retrofitted.

A fix_operands backend-legalization pass for x86 memory-to-memory constraints existed, but it was a no-op stub discovered and redesigned reactively (changed to return Vec) rather than designed cleanly — foresight present but partial.

Trajectory ends still stuck in basic compile/codegen bugs; no advanced feature (struct layout, typedef, switch) is observed landing, so the architecture's foresight is never validated by features slotting in cleanly.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent deliberately chose a canonical, extensible compiler architecture — clear pass boundaries, a typed AST, a dedicated type-system module, a TACKY intermediate IR for type-aware codegen, symbol/scope handling in sema, and struct/union AST nodes present from day one — which clearly surpasses anchor 5's 'clean separation adequate for early milestones' and reaches toward anchor 8's 'core representations designed with the later hard features in mind.' However, it does not earn a full 8/10 because the trajectory never demonstrates the advanced features actually slotting in without rewrites, and some backend structure (fix_operands legalization) was improvised reactively rather than anticipated. A 7 reflects strong, foresightful design intent that is not yet validated by later features landing cleanly.

rubric.task_read: This is an extreme long-horizon build: a from-scratch C compiler in Rust spanning lexer, full preprocessor, parser, semantic analysis, and x86-64 codegen, plus many advanced features (structs/unions, switch/case, typedef/casts, globals, short-circuit eval), gated by 780 tests across three real-world suites that must all pass. Difficulty comes from sheer scope, deep interdependence between passes, an implicit contract (C semantics + x86-64 ABI) the agent must recover, and the near-certainty that naive early design decisions will break under later features. A skilled practitioner would invest heavily and continuously in every meta-work faculty — deep orientation, staged milestones tied to test subsets, relentless test-driven verification, accurate pass-rate tracking, and willingness to refactor architecture mid-flight.

dimensions.name: C-semantics, ABI & test-suite orientation
dimensions.description: Understanding C language semantics, the x86-64 System V ABI/assembly conventions, and the structure/content of the three test suites before and while building.
dimensions.why_it_matters: The 'spec' is largely implicit — correct behavior is defined by C semantics, the calling convention, and what the 780 tests actually exercise. Acting without recovering this contract guarantees rework across nearly every pass.

anchors.0: Starts emitting code with no inspection of the test suites, run_tests.sh, or ABI conventions; guesses at behavior.
anchors.3: Skims run_tests.sh and writes a trivial hello-world compile; no systematic look at what features the tests demand or how the ABI/relocation works.
anchors.5: Reads run_tests.sh, samples tests from each suite, and establishes the basic x86-64 calling convention and assembly emission path before building core codegen.
anchors.8: Systematically categorizes tests by feature/difficulty, extracts the concrete language subset required, and probes ABI edge cases (struct passing, sizes/alignment, relocations) by compiling small reference cases; orientation directly shapes the build order.
anchors.10: Sustained, iterative research: continually mines failing tests to infer exact semantic requirements (integer promotion, evaluation order, layout rules), verifies assumptions against the assembler/linker behavior, and maintains a living understanding of the target contract that anticipates features before they are reached.

dimensions.name: Feature staging & milestone structure
dimensions.description: Breaking the compiler into an ordered hierarchy of passes and feature milestones, each with an explicit done-check (e.g. a passing test subset).
dimensions.why_it_matters: You cannot build all of C at once; the difference between steady progress and thrashing is a sane dependency-ordered plan (expressions before control flow before types before structs) with checkpoints.

anchors.0: No decomposition; attempts the whole compiler as one undifferentiated push or jumps between unrelated features at random.
anchors.3: Vague ordering ('do lexer, then parser, then codegen') with no feature-level milestones or explicit completion criteria.
anchors.5: Clear pass structure plus a feature roadmap in a reasonable dependency order, with milestones loosely tied to getting some tests passing.
anchors.8: Fine-grained, dependency-aware milestones each bound to a concrete test subset as its done-signal, sequenced so each milestone builds on verified prior ones; ordering reflects which features unlock the most tests.
anchors.10: A living milestone hierarchy that is re-prioritized as data arrives — smallest-viable-slice ordering, explicit gating criteria per milestone, and deliberate deferral of hard/rare features until foundations are proven, sustained coherently across the whole horizon.

dimensions.name: Test-driven verification design
dimensions.description: Deliberately building/using checks — incremental runs of test subsets, minimal repro cases, diffing against expected behavior — rather than assuming generated code is correct.
dimensions.why_it_matters: With 780 opaque pass/fail tests and a compiler where any pass can silently miscompile, a disciplined verification loop is the only way to know progress is real and to localize defects.

anchors.0: Never runs the tests until the very end, or writes code with no way to confirm correctness; assumes success.
anchors.3: Runs the full suite occasionally as the only check; no isolation of failures, no smaller probes.
anchors.5: Runs relevant test subsets after each feature and uses the pass/fail signal to guide fixes.
anchors.8: Builds a tight loop: reduces failing tests to minimal reproductions, inspects generated assembly, and compares against known-correct output to pinpoint which pass is wrong before editing.
anchors.10: Engineers verification infrastructure beyond what's handed over — categorized/scriptable subset runs, regression guards so fixed tests stay fixed, and root-cause isolation that distinguishes lexer/parser/sema/codegen defects — sustaining fast, trustworthy signal across the entire build.

dimensions.name: Pass-rate tracking & thrash detection
dimensions.description: Maintaining an accurate done-vs-remaining picture (which tests/features pass), and detecting regressions, circular debugging, or stalls across a very long horizon.
dimensions.why_it_matters: Over hundreds of features and edits, it is easy to lose the plot, regress previously-passing tests, or loop on one stubborn failure; an accurate live picture is what sustains net forward motion.

anchors.0: No sense of how many tests pass or which features remain; edits blindly with no scoreboard.
anchors.3: Occasional whole-suite counts but no tracking of trends, regressions, or which categories are outstanding.
anchors.5: Keeps a running tally of pass counts by suite/feature and notices when a change breaks previously-passing tests.
anchors.8: Maintains a structured, current view of pass rate by category and remaining work, and recognizes when stuck on one test — bounding effort and moving on rather than looping.
anchors.10: Treats pass-rate as a managed signal: detects regressions immediately and attributes them, spots circular/thrashing debugging early and deliberately changes tactics, and continuously re-derives the highest-leverage remaining work from the scoreboard.

dimensions.name: Design revision under falsified assumptions
dimensions.description: Revising architecture, data structures, or approach when a later feature (types, structs, ABI detail) exposes that an earlier design cannot support it.
dimensions.why_it_matters: Compilers are notorious for early choices (untyped AST, ad-hoc register allocation, string-based codegen) that collapse under types/structs; the ability to recognize and refactor rather than pile hacks decides whether the tail of the task is reachable.

anchors.0: Barrels ahead on a broken design, piling special-cases and hacks even as failures compound.
anchors.3: Patches symptoms locally; resists structural change even when the same class of bug keeps recurring.
anchors.5: When an approach clearly fails, reworks the affected component and re-verifies rather than forcing it.
anchors.8: Recognizes when a limitation is architectural (not local), makes a deliberate refactor (e.g. adding type info through the AST/IR), and confirms the change unblocks the stuck feature class.
anchors.10: Proactively detects design strain before it becomes a wall, weighs refactor-vs-workaround explicitly, executes larger restructurings cleanly while protecting already-passing tests, and updates the plan/design record so the correction propagates instead of recurring.

dimensions.name: Compiler architecture & IR foresight
dimensions.description: Choosing pass boundaries and core data structures (AST/IR, symbol tables, type representation) with enough foresight to accommodate the full required feature set rather than painting into a corner.
dimensions.why_it_matters: Unlike generic decomposition (what to do when) or adaptation (fixing after breakage), this is the upfront design judgment specific to compilers: a representation that anticipates types, structs, and the ABI avoids the most expensive class of rework on this task.

anchors.0: No deliberate architecture; monolithic, ad-hoc string-munging with no separable passes or reusable structures.
anchors.3: Minimal structure that works for the first trivial cases but has no provision for types, scopes, or layout.
anchors.5: Clean separation of lexer/parser/sema/codegen with data structures adequate for the early feature milestones.
anchors.8: Core representations (typed AST/IR, symbol/scope tables, type/layout model) are designed with the later hard features in mind, so structs/typedef/switch slot in without wholesale rewrites.
anchors.10: Architecture demonstrably anticipates the full contract — extensible IR and type system, clear invariants between passes — enabling most advanced features to be added additively; foresight is evidenced by later features landing cleanly rather than by luck.
